requirements.requirement: Run independent Prometheus replicas on node1 and node2 that collect host metrics from all four nodes.
requirements.summary: Both replicas were active and enabled with distinct local TSDB blocks, successful Thanos uploads, and zero upload failures. Each directly reported all four node-exporter targets healthy, and the final Thanos query returned node identity metrics for node1 through node4.

requirements.requirement: Provide operational Thanos Query, Store Gateway, and Compactor services on node3.
requirements.summary: All three services were active and enabled on node3 with their expected listeners. Store connections had no errors, compaction completed with zero failures and no halt condition, and the populated bucket passed verification.

requirements.requirement: Provide an authenticated HTTPS object store on node4:9000 using bucket thanos-metrics and storing data under /srv/thanos-objectstore.
requirements.summary: MinIO was active and enabled on port 9000 with a certificate valid for node4 and its managed IP. HTTPS health returned 200, anonymous bucket access returned 403 AccessDenied, authenticated access found 33 objects including nine block metadata files, and persistent files occupied /srv/thanos-objectstore.

requirements.requirement: Place the object-store access variables in /root/thanos-objectstore.env on node3.
requirements.summary: The root-owned mode-0600 file contained populated access-key and secret-key variables plus the required HTTPS endpoint and thanos-metrics bucket. Thanos was configured to verify the supplied CA with insecure mode disabled.

requirements.requirement: Serve queries on node3:10902 with replica deduplication.
requirements.summary: The same live query returned eight replica series with deduplication disabled and four series with default deduplication, with the replica label removed. The final audit again returned four healthy deduplicated host series on port 10902.

requirements.requirement: Retain current and historical query results when either Prometheus server is unavailable, followed by recovery.
requirements.summary: A healthy baseline showed both Prometheus endpoints ready and four healthy current and historical series. During separate bounded outages of node1 and node2, the stopped replica was directly unreachable, the other remained healthy, and both main-query and object-store-only historical probes returned four healthy series. Each replica was restored, after which both endpoints, query results, history, and StoreAPI connections were healthy again.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The captured evidence directly demonstrates the final service topology, authenticated TLS object storage, populated historical storage, query deduplication, and complete baseline-disruption-restoration-recovery transitions for loss of either Prometheus replica. Only minor temporary-file residue reduced operational hygiene.
limitations: Historical continuity was tested at one specific recent timestamp, including an object-store-only query, rather than across a long retention interval.
No reboot, simultaneous loss of both Prometheus replicas, or node3/node4 outage was observed; these scenarios were not explicitly required by the task.
Lifecycle hygiene observations are bounded inventories and do not exhaustively inspect every filesystem location.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final services had no failed units, package-manager consistency checks remained healthy, and temporary credential-transfer keys were removed. The deduction is for executor-created residue: 28 query JSON/log artifacts remained under /tmp on node3 and two response files remained on node4.
